AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: Although, miR-218 has been implicated in epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition process, the detailed mechanisms of miR-218 involvement in epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition in human lung adenocarcinoma cell are still unclear.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIALS & METHODS
AbstractText.content: miR-218 function assays and its target gene analysis were performed.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: miR-218 suppresses human lung adenocarcinoma cell migration and invasion and inhibits its target gene, Ecop and Robo1 expression, which subsequently suppresses NF-κB activity and its downstream targets.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: miR-218 inhibits human lung adenocarcinoma cell migration and invasion via the suppression of Ecop and Robo1 expression, thus suggesting that miR-218 could serve as a potential therapeutic target.
